summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic ER+ breast cancer involving the liver and bones was admitted with acute nausea, vomiting, and right-sided abdominal pain, consistent with a flare of her known gastroparesis. She had been unable to tolerate oral intake since the day before admission and presented with hypokalemia and elevated lactate. Imaging showed a mildly dilated bowel loop without obstruction. She was treated with IV fluids, electrolyte replacement, and anti-nausea medications including IV metoclopramide, ondansetron, and prochlorperazine. Her symptoms resolved, and she transitioned to oral metoclopramide three times daily. She received scheduled palliative radiation for bone metastases during admission and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned with gastroenterology.
problems: Secondary malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile duct
